To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of different clustering methods is comparable in terms of accuracy.

1) The use of clustering for cancer subtype discovery is an important tool for cancer research, 2) There is no single best clustering method, 3) Different clustering methods have different advantages and disadvantages, and 4) The choice of the clustering method depends on the specific research question.

(1) clustering methods based on gene expression data perform better than clustering methods based on clinical data; and (2) clustering methods based exclusively on gene expression data are not able to identify cancer subtypes that are biologically relevant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the most appropriate clustering methods for the analysis of gene expression data?
the following questions: (i) How do clustering algorithms compare to each other?
evaluating clustering methods in a comparative way, and with identifying the most appropriate clustering method(s) for cancer subtype discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of clustering algorithm is not important.
the best method is the one that is most appropriate to the data.

the use of classic clustering methods is not necessarily better than the use of more advanced methods, and that the use of a specific method is dependent on the type of data and the goal of the analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have performed a comparative study on clustering cancer gene expression data, and we have found that the use of clustering methods is not as straightforward as one would expect, and that the choice of a clustering method is not as important as the choice of the parameters of the clustering method.
we performed a large-scale evaluation on clustering cancer gene expression data and we have identified that the use of a hierarchical clustering method is the most suitable for this purpose.
we have performed a large-scale evaluation and comparison of different clustering algorithms for cancer subtypes discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single method that is superior to the others.
the choice of a clustering method is not a trivial task.
the choice of the method should be guided by the type of data and the type of analysis to be performed.
